title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8: Do not stretch the word grace beyond just limits—Pelagian abuse
pass_a_gloss: This one thing, however, I premise to be observed by you. When we say that the orthodox Fathers, who stood in the battle-line against Pelagius and the Pelagians, do not admit that grace is given to all on account of respect to the death of Christ, the word Grace (which the Pelagians formerly did) is not to be stretched beyond its just limits. For whatever is granted to human beings gratuitously by God can in some sense be called grace.
pass_b_english: One caution first. When we say the orthodox Fathers who fought Pelagius refuse to grant that grace is given to all merely because of Christ's death, we are not letting the word grace run loose past its proper bounds—the very move the Pelagians once made. Anything God freely grants to people can, in a loose sense, be called grace.
source_text: Hoc unum tamen praemitto a vobis observandum. Quando dicimus Patres orthodoxos, qui in acie steterunt contra Pelagium et Pelagianos, non admittere gratiam omnibus dari propter respectum ad mortem Christi, Gratiae vocabulum (quod Pelagiani olim faciebant) extra justos suos limites non esse extendendum. Quicquid enim gratiose hominibus conceditur a Deo, potest aliquo sensu gratia appellari.
